verdicts.item: Refutation: can the new type filter drop a GENUINE job entry that omits `type`?
verdicts.evidence: No. The predicate keeps `u.type == null`, so an untyped entry is retained, and the pre-existing green test at spec:1074 (`REG-B177: an ORS response with unassigned jobs keeps the primary solver`) drives exactly that shape — `unassigned: [{ id: 3 }]` with no `type` — and still resolves through the primary solver under the re-gate (`npx jest src/route-optimization src/routes` 244/244). Vroom can only report entries for what we sent, and `body.jobs` (:1347-1355) sends jobs only, so a type-less entry is necessarily a job. Worst case for a wrongly-dropped entry is a short count → the existing mismatch throw → nearest-neighbour fallback, never a wrong stop persisted.

verdicts.item: Pin discrimination: `REG-B177: only \`job\` entries of an ORS unassigned array index into the stop list` (spec:1198)

Without the filter, break id 3 resolves onto stops[2] and the call resolves to ["stop-1","stop-2","stop-3"] instead — which is precisely what the executor's self-probe recorded ("Received promise resolved instead of rejected / Resolved to value: [\"stop-1\", \"stop-2\", \"stop-3\"]"). newHazards.summary: The seed effect's comment claims "a time the operator chose survives a reopen ... the same shape" as templates/[id]/page.tsx, but on THIS page the reset effect (:126-139) clears `startTime` and `startTimeRef.current` on every open, so a chosen time never survives a reopen here and the two modals are not the same shape. The code is correct — the guard's real (and useful) job on this page is to stop a late-arriving `routeSettings.defaultStartTime` from clobbering a time the operator typed while settings were still loading — but the comment describes behaviour the file does not have, and a maintainer trusting it could "restore parity" by weakening the reset effect. Fix is a one-line comment correction, not a code change.

The guard cannot tell an operator-chosen time from an auto-seeded one, so a changed tenant default no longer reaches this always-mounted modal. Once any open seeds `defaultStartTime` (say 08:00), the field stays non-empty for the life of the page; if the owner then changes the tenant default to 09:00, every subsequent open of this modal keeps showing 08:00 until a full page reload, and a dispatch sends the stale value. Round 3 re-seeded on each open, so this is a new consequence of the round-4 guard. Low impact — the stale value is visible in the field, not silent — and tracking "seeded vs typed" (e.g. clearing `startTimeRef` when the field still equals the last seeded default) would resolve it if the owner cares.

recheck.reasoning: Both targeted hazards are genuinely closed and the round is narrow. Hazard [0]: the filter is the exact shape the review asked for, keeps untyped entries (so it cannot drop a real job — proven by the pre-existing green `{ id: 3 }` fixture at spec:1074, not just by reading), and leaves the sort/dedupe/mismatch-throw path byte-identical. Its pin carries a real value oracle in half (b), and the executor's self-probe (deleting only the filter line, exact-string, with sha256 restore verification) showed it going red on a resolved-vs-rejected value rather than an existence check. Hazard [3]: the templates modal is always mounted and has no reset effect, so the `startTimeRef` guard does exactly what was asked; the round-3 requirement that an emptied field stay empty still holds in both modals because `seededRef` short-circuits first and `startTime` was correctly kept out of the deps. The routes/page.tsx ordering dependency the executor flagged is real but sound — the reset effect is declared first and writes the ref synchronously, so the seed effect reads the cleared value in the same passive-effect flush. Render-body ref mirroring (`startTimeRef.current = startTime`) is against React's letter but matches existing house precedent in this app (inventory/page.tsx:910, orders/_components/CreateOrderModal.tsx:283), so I am not raising it. No probe residue in the tree; re-gate is green across api tsc, 244 api tests, web tsc and web lint. The two new hazards are both minor and non-blocking: one is a comment that overclaims parity between the modals, the other is a stale-tenant-default consequence of the guard that is visible in the UI rather than silent. Residuals [1] and [2] are untouched and not regressed. Nothing here warrants another round.
